label: Game 1
title: Men's Doubles Gold, 2026 US Open Pickleball — Game 1

source.note: Game 1 only. Events observed from the video. rally_number and point_number restart at 1 inside this game.

definitions.estimates: Speeds, positions, and reaction times are visual estimates from the video, in meters and seconds.
definitions.server: The player who hit shot 1 of the rally, when that contact is logged as a serve.
definitions.rally_winner: Scored rallies go to the point winner. Rallies with no point go to the receiving team (side-out scoring).
definitions.serve_points_won: Rallies served by the team that scored a point for it.
definitions.side_outs: Rallies received by the team that it won, taking the serve back.
definitions.deep: A serve or return that lands within 1.5 m of the baseline.
definitions.kitchen_landing: An in-bounds bounce in a kitchen zone. Only logged bounces count; a ball volleyed out of the air has none.
definitions.kitchen_arrival: Rallies where one of the player's moves ends at their own kitchen line (up to 0.75 m behind it), out of rallies they appear in.
definitions.lanes: Left, middle, and right thirds of the court width, as seen in the video.
definitions.targeted: Opponent shots this player answered, out of those their team answered.
definitions.first_attack: The first contact in a rally logged as an attack.
definitions.rally_length: Buckets of logged shots. Long dink exchanges were sampled, so counts are a lower bound.

data_quality.detail: Rallies whose first logged contact is not a serve. Their server and rally winner are unknown.
Points won by the receiving team. Only the serving team scores, so the server or the winner is wrong. Serve and side-out rates use the logged serve.
Points whose server_player_id is not the player who hit the serve.
Volleys and overheads hit after the previous shot bounced. A volley is hit before the bounce, so placement or shot type is wrong.
Back-to-back contacts by one team. The ball crosses the net between contacts, so contacts are missing. Shot counts are a lower bound.
Errors credited to the team that won the rally. An error ends the rally for the team that makes it.
Player moves centred on the opponents' half. Either the team end or the position is wrong, which skews kitchen arrival.
Reaction times that do not equal contact_sec minus stimulus_sec.
Reaction times have a standard deviation of 0.236 s. Below 0.05 s they look filled in rather than measured.
